title: Berlin Sauna Guide - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin sells sauna time in blocks, and the blocks are different sizes at every venue.** That is why there is no single cheapest place. Decide how long your gap is first, then pick, because the answer flips at about three and a half hours.

**The cheapest saunas in the city are shut right now.** Every public pool sauna is closed for the summer season and the operator reopens them on **1 November 2026**. Until then the 13 to 20 euro option simply does not exist.

**Short visit, go to Liquidrom.** Two hours in the thermal bath is 24.50 euros and the sauna area adds 2.50, so **27.00 euros** total. Möckernstraße 10 in Kreuzberg, two minutes from S Anhalter Bahnhof, open to midnight and to 01:00 on Friday and Saturday.

**Long visit, go to vabali.** Four hours is **36.50 euros** on a weekday and the day pass is 51.50. Seydlitzstraße 6 in Moabit, eight minutes on foot north of Hauptbahnhof. Weekends, public holidays and the Christmas period all cost 3 to 5 euros more.

**The sauna is textile free everywhere.** Berlin's public bath house rules state in English that the sauna areas may only be used naked. Venues differ only in how far that reaches: **vabali bans swimwear in the whole building**, while Liquidrom, Oderberger and the public baths want swimwear in the water and nothing in the hot room.

**Stadtbad Oderberger is a fixed two hour slot you book online.** Swim plus sauna is about 20 to 22 euros, the sauna is 18 plus and bookable from 11:00, and there is a **20 euro cash deposit** for the key card. The hall is also an event space, so it closes on event days and the timetable is only published two weeks ahead.
**Take two towels.** One to sit on in the sauna is compulsory at every venue, plus one to dry with. vabali also requires a bathrobe or kimono and bathing shoes outside the water.
**Thermen am Europa-Center is gone.** The Kurfürstendamm rooftop bath closed in 2020 and never reopened, but directory sites still list it. Check the operator's own page rather than an aggregator.
